records.name: Philadelphia Youth Orchestra Music Institute
records.summary: The music school of the Philadelphia Youth Orchestra. It gives music education to young players through auditioned ensembles and lessons.
records.what_you_do: Audition for one of the youth ensembles, or try a summer camp. You can also study an instrument with the institute. Anyone can attend the public concerts or sign up for the newsletter.

schedule.text: The flagship orchestra rehearses on Saturday mornings, 8:30 am to noon, from mid-September to early June. Other ensembles keep their own calendars, and concerts are posted on the events page.

cost.text: Flagship orchestra tuition is $2,195 a year for the 2026 to 2027 season. A $550 deposit is due at registration, after the audition, and is not refundable. Financial aid is available after the audition for students who show need.

first_step.how: Pick an ensemble on the auditions page, submit the online audition form with your preferred date and time, then wait for the office to confirm your appointment.
first_step.basis: Every ensemble starts with an audition booked by appointment, and registration comes only after the audition.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect an online form, then an audition booked by appointment. The flagship orchestra asks for scales, a solo of your choice and orchestral excerpts for your instrument. Its Saturday rehearsals run 8:30 am to noon, and the season's tuition is $2,195.
first_visit_tips: Practice the required scales, a solo of your choice, and the orchestral excerpts for your instrument before your audition.
Check the age range first: the flagship orchestra takes ages 15 to 22, and the Philadelphia Young Artists Orchestra takes ages 13 to 18.
Ask the office about financial aid, which comes after the audition for students who show need.
Check whether a concert needs a museum ticket; the jazz orchestra's Please Touch Museum show does.

records.notes: Ensemble ages differ between pages: the auditions page gives 11 to 17 for the Young Musicians Debut Orchestra and the programs page gives 12 to 17, so ages are left to the ensemble pages. Tuition for the other ensembles appeared only in a search summary, not on a page I read, so it is not recorded. The auditions page says applications for the 2026 to 2027 season are open. The Dec 5, 2026 concert is listed for 2 pm and 3 pm; the ticket link on that page points to a 2025 page and was not used.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Sports Collaborative
records.summary: A network of more than 170 youth sports programs across Philadelphia. It trains coaches and referees, shares safety guidance, and helps families find a sports program near home. It also works with the city on accessible recreation.
records.what_you_do: Families can search the member map by sport, then contact a program from its own website. Coaches, staff and volunteers from member groups can take free trainings (email membership@pysc.org). Groups can apply to join the network for free through its Apply Now form.

schedule.text: Events and trainings are posted on the events calendar with their own dates. Check the calendar for the current list.

cost.text: Searching the member map and joining the network are free. Trainings are free for coaches, staff and volunteers of member groups. Each sports program sets its own fees.

first_step.how: Open the Find A Provider member map, pick a sport tab, and contact a program from its own website.
first_step.basis: Families can search the member list and contact programs with no sign up, and the trainings ask for a simple email to join.
first_step.what_to_expect: The member map lists programs by sport and links to each program's own website. It does not show addresses, schedules, ages or fees, so families check each program before signing up. Coaches and volunteers can join free trainings on topics such as first aid, mandated reporting and trauma informed coaching.
first_visit_tips: Choose a sport tab first, since the map filters by sport only.
Check each program's own website for ages, schedule and fees.
The city's Program Locator covers city run recreation by age, activity, location and season.

records.notes: The member services page says membership has grown to over 200 organizations, while the become-a-member page says over 170 providers; the summary keeps 170. The training page names community members as an audience but says sessions are free for member staff and volunteers, so the record follows that narrower wording. PositiveCoach articles are linked from the parent page, but no URL for that group was checked, so it is not listed as a lead.

records.name: Philadelphia Zoo Volunteer Programs
records.summary: The Philadelphia Zoo runs several volunteer programs, from docent training to shifts at special events and internships in animal care and conservation education.
records.what_you_do: Train as a docent to lead visitor tours (21 and up, with about 50 service hours a year), work shifts at special events (13 and up for family events), join the teen Volun-TEENS program (14 to 17), or take a college internship.

schedule.text: Docent training runs over nine months in three modules, with new classes starting in spring, summer and January. Special event shifts run in the morning, afternoon or all day. Animal care and conservation interns work one to three days a week, depending on the term.

cost.text: Volunteering is unpaid, and the page lists no application fee. Volunteers get free admission and parking, plus food and gift shop discounts. Volunteers show proof of COVID vaccination or pay for weekly testing, per the page.

requirements.gear: Volunteers receive a free uniform shirt and ID badge.

first_step.how: Submit the online application for the program you want (docent, special events, Volun-TEENS or internship), then wait for the email that schedules your interview.
first_step.basis: Every program needs an online application, an interview, clearances and training before the first shift.
first_step.what_to_expect: After the interview you finish paperwork, a PA criminal background check and a child abuse clearance, plus fingerprinting if you lived outside Pennsylvania in the past 10 years. Next comes online orientation and onsite training that includes a zoo tour, and then you sign up for shifts. Most volunteer roles ask for a one year commitment.
first_visit_tips: Apply for a program that fits your age: docents are 21 and up, Volun-TEENS are 14 to 17, and special events take 13 and up for family events.
Plan for paperwork before your first shift, since shifts open only after you are cleared.
Ask the zoo about the background check for special events, because the page gives two different answers.
Most programs ask for a one year commitment, so decide before you apply.

records.notes: The zoo's page says special events volunteers are exempt from a criminal background check in one section, but its FAQ says all volunteers must provide one. background_check is set to true for that reason, and the zoo should confirm. The 13 minimum age is for family special events; the page gives 14 as the general minimum. The COVID vaccination or testing line may be out of date. The Volun-TEENS and school takeover contact email is hidden in the page and is not recorded. A July docent entry line shows a May 30 date that looks like a typo, so no entry dates are recorded beyond the season.

records.name: Philadelphia's Magic Gardens
records.summary: A mosaic art installation and museum on South Street, with guided tours, events, exhibitions and an artist residency. It also runs volunteer and membership programs.
records.what_you_do: Visit the mosaic installation during opening hours, or join a guided tour. Volunteers, who must be 18 or older, help with public programs, gallery installation and festival outreach. Families can join the Family Jams, hands-on art sessions on Sundays.

schedule.text: Open Wednesday to Monday, 11 am to 6 pm, and closed on Tuesdays. Morning Magic Tours start at 10 am on select dates. Family Jams run on Sundays from noon to 4 pm.

cost.text: Adults $15. Students, seniors 65 and up, and people with disabilities $12. Children 6 to 12 $8, and children 5 and under free. PMG members get in free. Tickets are timed and often sell out, so reserve online.

access.notes: Indoor galleries and parts of the sculpture garden are reachable, but the page calls wheelchair access somewhat limited. The tour basement and garden have narrow passages and stairs, and no ramp or elevator is listed. Loaner manual wheelchairs, a rollator and a cane chair go out first come, first served. Free sensory bags (noise canceling headphones, fidget toys, sunglasses) are at the front desk if you leave an ID, and reserving ahead is advised. Service animals are welcome on a leash. The pre-visit video has captions and an ASL interpreter. Touch tours for blind and low vision visitors, ages 14 and up, need a reservation.

first_step.how: Buy a timed ticket online for a visit during opening hours, Wednesday to Monday, 11 am to 6 pm.
first_step.basis: Open to the public at set hours with posted prices, though timed tickets often sell out. The site also lists tours, volunteering and membership.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is a timed, self-guided walk through the mosaic installation and museum. Staff can lend a folding chair on request, and sensory bags are available if you want them. Guided tours and Family Jams are also offered.
first_visit_tips: Reserve a timed ticket online before you come, since slots often sell out.
Last admission is 15 minutes before closing, and the site is closed on Tuesdays.
For sensory bags or other access help, call 215-733-0390 ext. 120 or email info@phillymagicgardens.org.
Family Jams are free with museum admission and run on Sundays from noon to 4 pm.

records.notes: Dropped the contact name 'The Organization' from tier 1, since it is a placeholder and not a person or office. Volunteer questions go to volunteer@phillymagicgardens.org per the volunteer FAQ. Parking and transit details sit behind a link that was not read, so none are recorded. The Family Jams page says the sessions are every second Sunday but lists dates four weeks apart, so the record says only Sundays. The Family Jams age range is not stated. Volunteer background checks and costs are not mentioned.

records.name: PhilHarmonia
records.summary: A Philadelphia choir of mixed voices, founded in 2013, that sings classical and modern a cappella music and gives concerts, some of them free.
records.what_you_do: Hear a concert, some of which are free. Singers join through an audition with a brief scales warmup, a tonal memory exercise, sight singing and a solo of their choice. Auditions for future seasons are planned for August 2027. You can join the mailing list or sign up for the audition list through a Google form linked on the site.

schedule.text: The choir gives concerts in the fall, winter and spring, and posts each date and place on its site. Rehearsal days and places are not on the public pages.

locations.label: Mailing address (also listed for mailed checks)

cost.text: Some concerts are free, and ticket prices for the others are not shown on the site. The site does not state dues or fees for singers.

first_step.how: Attend the free fall concert on November 7, 2026 at the Free Library's Parkway Central branch, or if you sing, fill in the audition list Google form linked from the site's auditions section.
first_step.basis: Hearing a concert is open to anyone, but joining the choir takes an audition, and the next one is planned for August 2027.
first_step.what_to_expect: A concert visit is simply attending the show. Evening concerts list doors at 7:30 pm and music at 8 pm, and the free fall concert runs twice, at 1:30 and 3:30 pm. Singers who want to join take a brief audition: scales, a tonal memory exercise, sight singing and an unaccompanied solo of their choice.
first_visit_tips: The free fall concert is at the Parkway Central branch of the Free Library, so plan the trip there.
Pick the 1:30 pm or 3:30 pm show for the fall concert.
For evening concerts, arrive at the 7:30 pm doors time.
Join the mailing list on the site to hear when auditions open.

records.notes: The concert venues named (Free Library Parkway Central, German Society of Pennsylvania) are event sites, not the group's address. The spring concert has no time or place yet. The site has no FAQ, no dues information and no rehearsal details, so none are recorded. An Eventbrite fundraiser link is for a single event and is not recorded.

records.name: Philly AI Connect
records.summary: A Philadelphia community for people interested in artificial intelligence and machine learning. It runs talks, speaker sessions, workshops, and networking, and welcomes volunteers and speakers.
records.what_you_do: Attend talks, summits and hands on AI demos. Volunteer, speak or sponsor through the forms on the events page, and use the group's Meetup page to find out about upcoming events. The group describes open source work on Discord.

schedule.text: The group holds talks, summits and workshops a few times a year. Dates are listed on its events page.

cost.text: Most event costs are not stated on the site. Check the event's own sign up link before you go.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer sign up form linked on the events page, or use the group's Meetup page to join for the next event.
first_step.basis: Events are open to the public and the site links to a way to join, but its homepage RSVP button has no working link.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events mix a talk or keynote with questions and answers, live AI demos, networking and food from sponsors, according to the group's site. Venue and cost are often not stated, so check each event's own page. Some events use an RSVP page on another platform, so register there before you go.
first_visit_tips: Register through the event's own link, since some events use a separate RSVP platform.
Check the events page for the venue, because it is often not stated.

records.notes: No upcoming events were clearly dated on the site today. Three sessions on the events page carry short numeric dates (for example 02:18:26) that look like early 2026 or cannot be read, so they are not recorded as upcoming. The (Co)nnect summit appears both with an RSVP link and under past events dated May 7, 2026, so it is not recorded as upcoming. The homepage mentions Discord for open source work, but the contact page lists no Discord. The Meetup page was used only as a link on the group's own site, not as a source of facts.

records.name: Philly Dance Share
records.summary: A volunteer-run dance collective that offers affordable weekly classes for adult dancers at every level.
records.what_you_do: Take a weekly class (contemporary, floorwork, multimedia movement or a workshop series), pay what you can when you register, or ask about teaching a class. Email the group to get involved.

schedule.text: Weekly classes: Mondays 7 to 8:30 pm and Wednesdays 10 to 11:30 am at Mascher Space, and Thursdays 7 to 8:30 pm and Saturdays 11 am to 12:30 pm at & Space. Each class runs 90 minutes.

cost.text: Pay what you can. Each class offers a price from $0 to $20, and no one is turned away for lack of funds. Floorwork suggests $15 to $20. An optional $1 donation covers card fees. Payments are not refundable, but you can email before class to move a payment to another class.

requirements.gear: Floorwork classes ask for long sleeves and pants, with knee pads recommended. Masks are optional for most classes.

access.notes: The site asks people with access needs to email the group before class.

first_step.how: Pick a class on the class schedule page, register online ahead of time, and choose the amount you can pay when you sign up.
first_step.basis: The site says classes take everyone from absolute beginner up, a levels guide points beginners to the beginner class, and the site explains how to register online.
first_step.what_to_expect: The classes are contemporary, experimental or floorwork based, and most run 90 minutes. The collective is artist led, and the schedule lists levels such as all levels, beginner intermediate or intermediate. The Pixelations workshop needs no movement experience.
first_visit_tips: Wear long sleeves and pants for floorwork classes, and consider knee pads, which the site recommends.
Classes meet at & Space, 1021 Hamilton Street, third floor (some listings say room 302), or at Mascher Space, 1170 South Broad Street.
Email phillydanceshare@gmail.com before class to move a payment to another class or to ask about access needs.
Masks are optional for most classes.

records.notes: Interest changed from social_dance (tier 1) because the site lists no social dance, only contemporary, experimental and floorwork classes. dance_company is the closest tag in the vocabulary, since no contemporary dance tag exists. Some class listings carry date typos (a Thursday 9/10 label on classes dated October 8 and October 15), so the record uses only the weekly pattern. Drop-in rules are stated for one series only, so drop_in is left out. No prices are listed per class beyond the pay what you can range.
